chapter: King Oliver, own trio and Kirby
title: Trio repertoire at the Victoria: In the Mood and Swing
summary: The Moore-Brown-Frye trio played Benny Goodman material and Swing tunes, with Brown on alto and Frye on piano.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Well, let's get into talking about the Pete Brown-Don Frye-Fred Moore trio. You were the leader.
Yes.
And you played at the Victoria.
Yes.
What were some of the...? Do you remember some of the tunes you played? Did you take requests from the audience? Or did you have a repertoire...?
Well, we had... We played numbers like 'In The Mood'...
Moore (II) - 40
"In The Mood," uh-huh.

We played a lot of Benny Goodman stuff. "In The Mood" and "Tuxedo Junction" and... We couldn't do too much with them, but we played two or three choruses. We just happened to have had a good saxophone; Pete Brown was a good saxophone player...
He was an alto player.
Yeah.
Was he popular at that time?
Oh yeah. He used to work at a dance hall, dance school.
[PAUSE]
...Don Frye..
Yeah, he was a good pianist.
What were some of the special characteristics of their playing that you liked in particular?
Nothing particular. Because we played all the Swing stuff.
Because "In The Mood" was supposed to have originated with Ernie Fields.
That's Benny Goodman, he recorded...
He's the one who recorded it and made it possible.
Yes.
